name: Insulin glargine
route_note: subcutaneous injection once daily (100 U/mL or concentrated 300 U/mL pens)
owner: Sanofi (biosimilars from Lilly, Biocon/Viatris and others)

discovery.note: Engineered in the 1990s by substituting glycine at A21 and adding two arginines to the B-chain C-terminus, shifting the isoelectric point.

tagline: First once-daily basal insulin analogue; it precipitates under the skin for a flat profile
summary: Insulin glargine is a long-acting insulin analogue that provides basal insulin cover for about 24 hours after a single subcutaneous injection. Marketed as Lantus from 2000, it became the world's best-selling insulin; biosimilars including the first interchangeable biosimilar, Semglee, are now available.
mechanism: Glargine differs from human insulin by glycine at position A21 and two arginines added to the B chain. These changes raise the isoelectric point so that the clear acidic solution forms microprecipitates at the neutral pH of subcutaneous tissue, from which insulin dissolves slowly and steadily.

After absorption glargine is cleaved to active metabolites (M1, M2) that bind the insulin receptor and exert the same metabolic actions as human insulin: increased glucose uptake in muscle and fat and suppressed hepatic glucose production, with no pronounced peak.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus requiring basal insulin

history.title: Lantus approved
history.detail: FDA approves Lantus in April 2000 and the European Commission approves it in June 2000.

history.title: Cancer-signal controversy
history.detail: Observational studies prompt regulatory reviews of a possible cancer link; later data did not confirm an association.

history.title: ORIGIN trial
history.detail: The ORIGIN trial in over 12,000 people with dysglycaemia shows neutral cardiovascular outcomes for early glargine.

history.title: First biosimilar in Europe
history.detail: Lilly/Boehringer Ingelheim's Abasaglar becomes the first insulin biosimilar approved in the EU.

history.title: Toujeo and Basaglar
history.detail: FDA approves the concentrated 300 U/mL Toujeo and Lilly's follow-on Basaglar.

history.title: First interchangeable biosimilar
history.detail: In July 2021 FDA designates Semglee (insulin glargine-yfgn) the first interchangeable biosimilar in the US.

pk.half_life: duration of action about 24 h (U100), longer for U300
pk.bioavailability: slow, peakless absorption from SC depot
pk.metabolism: cleaved at the B-chain to active metabolites M1 and M2

facts: Semglee was the first biosimilar of any kind to be designated interchangeable by FDA (2021).
Glargine must not be diluted or mixed with other insulins, because changing the pH destroys its depot mechanism.

references.title: ORIGIN Trial Investigators. Basal insulin and cardiovascular outcomes (NEJM 2012)
